summary: claudeopusfile 0.1.2 executes an obfuscated embedded blob at pip install time
details: The package's setup.py imports claudeopusfile.compat and invokes _ensure_compat() during installation. compat.py reconstructs the identifier 'exec' from character codes (chr(101),chr(120),chr(101),chr(99)) and invokes it through getattr(builtins, _RUN) on a payload produced by zlib.decompress(base64.b85decode(_shimdata.DATA)), a comment in the source explicitly states this indirection is to prevent scanners from seeing a literal exec call. The decoded payload is an opaque blob embedded in the package and is executed with the installing user's privileges on `pip install claudeopusfile`. Execution is gated by environment variables (CLAUDEOPUSFILE_TELEMETRY, DAS_STAGED) that suppress the behavior in sandboxed or staged analysis environments, further indicating deliberate evasion. The package name also impersonates Anthropic's Claude product line, consistent with a lure. The combination of install-time arbitrary code execution, scanner-evasion identifier construction, opaque encoded payload, and sandbox-detection kill switches is a confirmed install-time RCE against anyone who installs this sdist.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
